notes: Node/edge graph model is plain JSON state — a Claude agent can CRUD entities/relationships by editing the nodes[]/edges[] arrays directly. Best-in-class interactive/aesthetic rendering and the de facto base layer for ERD builder apps (see NextERD). Diffing requires snapshotting the JSON state yourself (no built-in versioning); rendering needs a browser/React runtime, not pure CLI.

Purpose-built React ER-diagram component with i18n and modular entity organization. Narrower community than React Flow; good fit if the team wants ERD-specific affordances out of the box rather than building on a generic graph canvas.

Generator, not an editor — derives an ERD (Mermaid/SVG) from a Prisma schema file. Strong fit only if the Fivetran-landed tables are modeled in Prisma; CRUD means editing the .prisma source, then regenerating. Runs headlessly via CLI, git-diff friendly since output can be Mermaid text.

Text-based ERD editor (custom DSL) with drag-and-drop UI plus codegen for migrations/types/ORM entities. The DSL is a plain-text file an agent can CRUD directly and diff in git; visual editor is optional, not required.

erDiagram syntax is plain text — trivial for an agent to CRUD (add/rename entities, add relationship lines) and git-diffs cleanly line by line. Renders natively in GitHub/GitLab markdown and via mmdc CLI headlessly. Aesthetic ceiling is lower than React Flow/JointJS for very large or highly custom-styled graphs.
